source: Short stories for the places along the Rift, written from published sources (Kenya Wildlife Service, National Museums of Kenya, UNESCO, Wikipedia) and kept to what they agree on. Positions marked 'town' come from GeoNames; positions marked 'area' are the approximate centre of a park, lake or hill range, placed by hand on the terrain and to be corrected by the owner where he knows better. Kinds: wildlife, people, origins, landmark. A story with 'site' instead of lat and lon attaches to that route card's pin. 'life' lists the figures drawn at a place: kind, how many, how they move (herd, flock, solo, line or still), the ground they keep to in km, 'at' where they stand if not at the pin, and a note on why they are there and since when. They stand for the animals and people of a place, not for sightings.

places.title: The Kerio Valley
places.blurb: The Kerio flows north along the floor of the Rift between the Elgeyo escarpment and the Tugen Hills, about a thousand metres below Iten. The east face of the escarpment is the wall pilots soar, and the long flights run north and south along it.

places.title: Hell's Gate
places.blurb: A park of red cliffs, gorges and steam vents that can be crossed on foot or by bicycle among zebra, buffalo and giraffe. Olkaria, inside the park, is where Kenya draws geothermal power from the floor of the Rift.

life.name: Zebra
life.note: Zebra, buffalo, gazelle and giraffe graze the floor of the gorge among walkers and cyclists, which is possible because the park has no lions. It was gazetted in 1984.

places.title: Mount Longonot
places.blurb: A young stratovolcano with an intact crater nearly two kilometres across, climbed from the road in a few hours and walked around the rim in a few more. Its forest fills the crater floor.

places.title: Kijabe Hill
places.blurb: The eastern wall of the Rift above Mai Mahiu, with the old escarpment road below. At its foot stands the small chapel built by Italian prisoners of war in 1942 while they cut that road.

places.title: Ukambani
places.blurb: Machakos is the heart of Ukambani, the land of the Kamba, known for wood carving and basketry. The town was the first administrative centre of British East Africa, before Nairobi was founded.

places.title: The Chyulu Hills
places.blurb: A range of young volcanic cones and lava flows, the latest of them from the 1850s, with some of the longest lava tubes in the world beneath. The rain that falls here sinks through the lava and surfaces at Mzima Springs.

places.label: Lake Nakuru
places.title: Lake Nakuru
places.blurb: A soda lake ringed by acacia woodland, famous for its flamingos and now a fenced sanctuary for black and white rhino. With Elementaita and Bogoria it forms the Kenya Lake System, a World Heritage Site since 2011.

life.name: Flamingos
life.note: The flamingos feed on the algae that bloom in the soda water. Their numbers rise and fall with the lake: in the high water since 2013 most of them moved on to Bogoria, and they return as the lake drops.

life.name: Rhino
life.note: Black rhino were brought back to Nakuru after the park was fenced as a sanctuary in the late 1980s, and white rhino followed. It is one of the oldest rhino sanctuaries in Kenya.

places.label: Lake Bogoria
places.title: Lake Bogoria
places.blurb: A deep soda lake under the Siracho escarpment, with hot springs and geysers along its shore and, in a good season, vast flocks of lesser flamingo. Part of the Kenya Lake System World Heritage Site.

life.name: Lesser flamingos
life.note: Lesser flamingos feed on the blue-green algae of the hot soda water, and when Nakuru is too fresh for them they gather here in their hundreds of thousands. Counts at Bogoria have passed a million.

places.label: Lake Baringo
places.title: Lake Baringo
places.blurb: A freshwater lake on the floor of the Rift with hippo, crocodile and well over four hundred recorded bird species. The Njemps who fish it are among the few cattle-keeping peoples of the Rift who also take to the water.

life.name: Hippo
life.note: Hippo spend the day in the water and graze the shore at night; crocodiles bask on the banks. Baringo is fresh where its neighbours are soda, which is why both live here and not at Bogoria.

places.label: Lake Naivasha
places.title: Lake Naivasha
places.blurb: The highest of the Kenyan Rift lakes, and fresh, with hippo in the papyrus and fish eagles in the acacias. Crescent Island, the rim of a drowned crater, is walked on foot among giraffe and zebra.

life.name: Hippo
life.note: Hippo live in the papyrus along the shore and come out at night to graze. The giraffe and zebra of Crescent Island are walked among on foot, because nothing on the island hunts them.

places.label: Lake Elementaita
places.title: Lake Elementaita
places.blurb: A shallow soda lake where great white pelicans breed on the islets and flamingos feed, protected within the Soysambu conservancy. The third of the Kenya Lake System World Heritage lakes.

life.name: Flamingos
life.note: Flamingos feed in the shallows, and the islets are one of the few places in East Africa where great white pelicans breed.

places.label: Menengai
places.title: Menengai crater
places.blurb: A volcanic caldera on the edge of Nakuru, about twelve kilometres by eight, formed in a great eruption some eight thousand years ago, its floor a field of old lava. One of the largest calderas in the world.

places.label: Mount Suswa
places.title: Mount Suswa
places.blurb: A shield volcano with a crater inside a crater, the inner one ringed by a moat, and a system of lava caves beneath its slopes. Maasai herders graze its outer flanks.

places.label: Olorgesailie
places.title: Olorgesailie
places.blurb: A dry lake bed in the southern Rift where stone hand axes lie in their thousands, left by early humans over hundreds of thousands of years. Louis and Mary Leakey began excavating here in the 1940s; the site is open, with a small museum.

places.label: Kariandusi
places.title: Kariandusi
places.blurb: A prehistoric site above Gilgil where Louis Leakey found Acheulean hand axes and cleavers in 1928, one of the first such sites known in East Africa. A small museum stands beside the old diatomite mine.

places.label: Hyrax Hill
places.title: Hyrax Hill
places.blurb: A Neolithic and Iron Age settlement on a hill outside Nakuru, excavated by Mary Leakey in the late 1930s, with burial mounds and hut floors and a museum in the old farmhouse.

places.label: Tugen Hills
places.title: The Tugen Hills
places.blurb: The hills between the Kerio Valley and Lake Baringo, where the six-million-year-old fossils of Orrorin tugenensis were found in 2000, among the oldest candidates for the human line.

places.label: Home of Champions
places.title: Iten, Home of Champions
places.blurb: A town of runners at 2,400 m on the lip of the Elgeyo escarpment. The arch over its road calls it the Home of Champions: the Kalenjin athletes who train on its red tracks and roads have won a large share of the world's distance medals.

life.name: Runners
life.note: Runners train on the roads and tracks out of Iten from first light, at 2,400 m. Athletes have trained here in numbers since the 1970s, when Brother Colm O'Connell began coaching at St Patrick's High School.

places.label: Maasai country
places.title: Maasai country
places.blurb: The southern Rift from Suswa to Amboseli is Maasai land: pastoralists whose cattle, red cloth and beadwork are the best known image of Kenya, and who still move their herds across it.

life.name: Maasai cattle
life.note: Cattle are wealth and food to the Maasai, who moved south along the Rift between the fifteenth and the eighteenth centuries and still herd across it, from Kajiado to Amboseli and beyond.

places.label: Kikuyu highlands
places.title: The Kikuyu highlands
places.blurb: The slopes between the Aberdares and Mount Kenya are the heartland of the Kikuyu, the largest of Kenya's peoples: tea and coffee country, and the ground of the Mau Mau uprising of the 1950s, with Nyeri at its centre.

places.label: Marakwet furrows
places.title: The Marakwet furrows
places.blurb: Along the northern Elgeyo escarpment the Marakwet have watered the valley floor for centuries with furrows cut along the cliffs, a system still in use and still managed by the clans.

places.label: Rimoi
places.title: Rimoi and Lake Kamnarok
places.blurb: A small reserve on the floor of the Kerio Valley that elephants pass through on an old corridor up and down the Rift. Across the river, Lake Kamnarok was once thick with crocodiles; it has shrunk badly in recent years.

life.name: Elephants
life.note: Elephants pass through Rimoi on an old route up and down the Kerio Valley, and it was to keep that route open that the reserve was set aside in 1983.

places.label: Amboseli
places.title: Amboseli
places.blurb: Elephants under Kilimanjaro: a park of swamps and dust where the longest-running study of wild elephants has followed the same families since 1972.

life.name: Elephants
life.note: The elephants come to Amboseli for its swamps, fed by water that falls on Kilimanjaro and surfaces here in a dry plain. The families of this park have been followed by name since 1972, the longest study of wild elephants anywhere.

places.label: Mzima Springs
places.title: Mzima Springs
places.blurb: Springs in Tsavo West fed by rain that fell on the Chyulu Hills and filtered through their lava, pouring out clear enough to watch hippo and crocodile from an underwater hide.

life.name: Hippo
life.note: Hippo spend the day in the clear pools, and their dung feeds the fish that live on it, a chain the filmmakers Alan and Joan Root followed underwater here.

places.label: Kilimanjaro
places.title: Kilimanjaro
places.blurb: Africa's highest mountain at 5,895 m, across the border in Tanzania, its ice on the horizon from the Chyulu Hills on a clear morning.

places.label: Mount Kenya
places.title: Mount Kenya
places.blurb: The second highest mountain in Africa at 5,199 m, an old volcano with glaciers on its twin summits, Batian and Nelion. A World Heritage Site.

places.label: Nairobi park
places.title: Nairobi National Park
places.blurb: The only national park inside a capital city, gazetted in 1946 as Kenya's first, where rhino and lion graze against the skyline.

life.name: Lion
life.note: Lion hunt the plains within sight of the city's towers, and the park is one of Kenya's oldest sanctuaries for black rhino, which bred well enough here to stock other parks.

places.label: Ngong Hills
places.title: The Ngong Hills
places.blurb: Four knuckles of hill on the edge of the Rift. Karen Blixen farmed at their foot and wrote Out of Africa about it; a wind farm now runs along the ridge.

places.label: Thomson's Falls
places.title: Thomson's Falls
places.blurb: A 74 m fall on the Ewaso Ng'iro at Nyahururu, reached by the Scottish explorer Joseph Thomson in 1883 and named for his father.

places.label: Samburu
places.title: Samburu
places.blurb: A reserve on the Ewaso Ng'iro in dry country north of Mount Kenya, home to the Samburu special five: Grevy's zebra, reticulated giraffe, Somali ostrich, gerenuk and beisa oryx.

life.name: Reticulated giraffe
life.note: The reticulated giraffe and Grevy's zebra of Samburu are dry-country animals of the north, found in few other places; most of the world's remaining Grevy's zebra live in northern Kenya.

places.label: Ol Pejeta
places.title: Ol Pejeta
places.blurb: A conservancy on the Laikipia plateau that holds the last two northern white rhinos on earth, Najin and Fatu, under guard day and night.

life.name: Najin and Fatu
life.note: Najin and Fatu, the last two northern white rhinos, came here from a zoo in the Czech Republic in 2009; the last male, Sudan, died in 2018. Ol Pejeta also holds more black rhino than any other sanctuary in East Africa.

places.label: Lake Magadi
places.title: Lake Magadi
places.blurb: A soda lake at the hot southern end of the Rift, its surface a crust of trona that has been mined for over a century, with flamingos on the brine.

life.name: Flamingos
life.note: Flamingos feed in the lagoons at the edge of the lake, where hot springs bring water in over the crust of soda.

places.label: The Aberdares
places.title: The Aberdares
places.blurb: A range of moorland and forest where in February 1952 Princess Elizabeth went up to Treetops lodge a princess and came down a queen.

life.name: Buffalo
life.note: Buffalo and elephant come to the salt licks and waterholes under the forest lodges at night, which is what Treetops was built to watch in 1932.

places.label: The Equator
places.title: The Equator
places.blurb: The line crosses the road at Nanyuki, where a sign marks it, and again on the roads north of Nakuru. The tour drives across it on the way south from Kerio.

places.label: Baobab country
places.title: Baobab country
places.blurb: Between Kibwezi and Mtito Andei the Mombasa road runs through baobab country, the hot red lowlands of Tsavo. The trees stand bare for most of the year, their swollen trunks holding water through the dry months, and bear their fruit in hanging pods.

life.name: Baobabs
life.note: Baobabs stand in the hot lowlands of Tsavo and along the Mombasa road, where the rains are short and the trees hold water in their trunks. The big ones are counted in centuries, and the oldest dated trees in Africa are over two thousand years old.
